To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a stereo visual inertical odometry system that uses nonlinear optimization to fuse visual measurements with IMUs.

we present a stereo visual inertual odometry (VioStereo) which jointly combines stereo images with IMU measurements in a tightly coupled way, and that we perform feature tracking and matching using a KLT optical flow tracker and circular matching, respectively.

we present a robust, efficient, and accurate stereo visual inertial navigation system using nonlinear optimization and circular stereo matching, and that we compare the performance of stereo and monocular visual inertia odometry using the EuRoC dataset, and demonstrate that our method is competitive with the most advanced algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: 1) a stereo visual inertially-aided odometry system based on the nonlinear optimization framework; 2) the integration of accelerometer bias into the optimization process; 3) the use of a FAST feature detector and KLT sparse optical tracking to improve the efficiency; 4) circular matching between stereo image pairs to remove outliers in feature tracking; 5) experimental results that show our method exhibits competitive accuracy and robustness with the most advanced visual inertial odometries

a robust stereo VIO system can be implemented with a low-cost sensor setup, which can be useful in applications where size and cost are important factors.
